sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge
 Order

01. A simple meaning application has kept this Court engaged from December 2022 onwards for the purpose of sorting out as to how much interest component with respect to the enhanced compensation awarded in favour of the applicant/claimant is payable from the non- applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Company Limited.
02. This Court would like to identify the source of confusion for sorting out the matter.

03. The applicant/claimant - Ramesh Chander and three others came to file a claim petition No.
3/Claim on In 01.04.2005 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu.
04. The claim petition was filed on account of death of Kishore Sharma in a road traffic accident who was the son of applicant/claimant - Ramesh Chander.

Ramesh Chander & Ors vs United India Insurance Co on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53724891/
1 05.

sentences.text:
Since it was a death related claim petition, as such, statutory deposit of Rs. 50,000/-
accompanied with interest component of Rs. 2,917/- on 14.01.2006 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu which came to be withdrawn by the applicant/claimant.

06. Claim petition came to be disposed of by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu vide an award dated 31.12.2008 thereby awarding compensation of an amount of Rs. 4,11,000/- minus the interim compensation of Rs. 50,000/- already paid to the claimants.

The compensation of Rs.
4,11,000/- was made payable alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till actual realization.
The non- applicant - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., was made liable to discharge the liability of payment of awarded compensation.
07. The claim petition was filed on 01.04.2005 and, therefore, the interest calculation with respect to compensation In awarded was to commence from this date as per the terms of the award.

08. Aggrieved of the lesser side compensation granted in their favour, the claimants came forward with a miscellaneous appeal No. 51 of 2009 under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before this Court filed on 17.02.2009.
09.

On the other hand, the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., acting at its own discretion in acceptance of the award dated 31.12.2008 came forward with deposit of an amount of Rs. 5,15,088/- on 05.05.2009 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT),
Jammu towards purported discharge of the liability imposed in terms of said award dated 31.12.2008.
10.

The appeal filed by the claimants resulted in enhancement of compensation amount from Rs.
4,11,000/- to Rs. 7,04,000/- alongwith interest @ 7.5 % per annum w.e.f. date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 01.04.2005.
11.
Thus, the enhancement came to take place by an amount of Rs. 2,93,000/- in terms of the appellate judgment dated 22.09.2016 of this Court.
In this judgment, it came to be clearly stated that enhanced compensation to be paid alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum.
In 12.

Upon enhanced compensation of an amount of Rs.
2,93,000/-, interest @ 7.5% per annum w.e.f. date of filing of claim petition i.e. 01.04.2005 came out to be Rs. 2,58,582/- thereby making enhanced compensation amount alongwith interest accrued thereupon payable in favour of the claimants to be Rs. 5,51,582/-.

13. The non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co.
Ltd., came forward with deposit of an amount of Rs. 5,51,703/- which was rupees 121 more than actually payable.

This deposit came to be made with this Court on 05.01.2017 by the Ramesh Chander & Ors vs United India Insurance Co on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53724891/
2 non-applicant/respondent i.e. the Insurance Company.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Still aggrieved of the lesser amount of compensation enhanced in their favour in terms of the appellate judgment dated 22.09.2016, the claimants came forward with a review petition with respect to said judgment dated 22.09.2016 which resulted in rehearing of miscellaneous appeal MA No. 51/2009 and earning a final judgment dated 25.02.2022 wherein from the awarded amount of Rs. 7,04,000/- enhanced in terms of the judgment dated 22.09.2016, the compensation came to be enhanced to Rs. 12,39,600/- alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till the same is paid.
In 15.

Thus, up till enhancement of compensation to Rs.
7,04,000/- in terms of judgment dated 22.09.2016, the claimants had been paid the compensation amount enhanced alongwith interest and, as such, up till this phase there was no issue obtaining between the claimants and the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd..

16. As in terms of judgment in review dated 25.02.2022, enhancement came to take place from Rs.
7,04,000/- to Rs. 12,39,600/- so the differential compensation amount becoming payable in favour of the claimants came to be Rs. 5,35,600/- on which interest @ 7.5% per annum was also to be payable.
17.

Non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co.
Ltd., came to be taken by a confusion as to from which date the interest liability is to be computed that is from the date of review petition or from the date of the claim petition and for this purpose applicants/claimants came forward with an application CM No. 7716/2022 which resulted in clarification coming forth from the Court that an interest @ 7.5% per annum payable would be on the enhanced compensation amount to Rs. 5,35,600/- and is to be from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 01.04.2005.

This In clarification came forward in terms of an order dated 01.11.2023.
18.

As per the claimants, the interest component on the enhanced compensation of Rs. 5,35,600/- @
7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 01.04.2005 was supposed to come to Rs. 6,89,493/- upto 31.05.2022 on which date the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., had come to deposit Rs. 6,37,291/- payable towards enhanced compensation of Rs. 5,35,600/- alongwith the interest calculated thereupon by the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., as per its own calculation which was based upon the fact that interest @ 7.5% was calculated from 24.10.2019 to 05.05.2022 aggregating to Rs. 1,01,691/- added to Rs. 5,35,600/- totaling to Rs. 6,37,291/-.
19.

Thus, in a sense, the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., calculated the interest on enhanced compensation for a period of 2 years whereas as per the claimants the Ramesh Chander & Ors vs United India Insurance Co on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53724891/
3 calculation of the interest on enhanced compensation amount of Rs. 5,35,600/- ought to have been w.e.f. 01.04.2005 which by the calculation as done by the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., for 2 years period would come about to Rs. 6,89,493/- as calculated by the learned counsel for In the claimants thereby entitling the claimants to earn interest component amount of Rs. 5,87,802/- upto 31.05.2002 and from there onwards an additional amount interest component of Rs. 93,605/- by being added making total interest payable in favour of the claimants to Rs. 6,81,407/- which is still remaining to be payable by the non-applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., in favour of the claimants.
20.

sentences.text: Today, Mr. Ravinder Sharma, learned counsel for the non- applicant/respondent - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., is not available for enabling this Court to clinch this matter.
On his behalf, Advocate Mr. Maninder Pal Singh Bijral present seeks an adjournment.

21. Adjourned.
22. List CM No. 7716/2024 on 27.09.2024.
